clue.text: Roughly handled, but quietly impressed

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to be impressed is to be filled with awe, i.e. awed

explanation.surface: Someone was manhandled but kept their admiration to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or clumsy person that has pawed something has touched it with rough, groping hands.

clue.text: Quick, by gum! No way horse can be held

indicators.note: these pieces are held within the word for gum, gripped inside it

parts.note: paste is an adhesive like gum
O is nought, a nil or no score
ST is street, a way
H is slang for heroin, also called horse

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a horse can be held in no way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by gum!' looks like a northern English oath, but gum is the glue holding O, ST and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb for with all speed, originally a direction on urgent letters.

clue.text: Shakespeare employed English composer

indicators.note: to employ is to take on, so the bard's name takes in the letter

parts.note: Will is William Shakespeare's first name

explanation.surface: The Bard hired an English composer for his plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Weill was the German-born composer of The Threepenny Opera.

clue.text: As constable, do good by stopping sin

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a stopping fills a gap, so one word plugs another and they sit together, one inside

parts.note: to err is to sin or stray

explanation.surface: A policeman preaches virtue by putting a stop to wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link. The surface reads 'stopping sin' as preventing wrongdoing, but 'stopping' means plugging a gap, one word filling the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogberry is the bumbling constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.

clue.text: I don't understand that return invitation

explanation.surface: A puzzled reply and an invitation to visit again.
explanation.definitionFit: Said with a frown it asks a speaker to repeat themselves; said warmly at the door it invites a guest back for another visit.

clue.text: Pen students shouldn't use

explanation.surface: A writing pen that pupils are banned from using.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a stall or enclosure for animals, and also a cheat sheet or translation copied from illicitly.

clue.text: Champagne with fresh soup is one's finest creation

parts.note: a magnum is a double-sized bottle, often of champagne

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters are remade in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A celebratory bottle of champagne alongside new soup is a chef's masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for great work, the phrase names an artist's most important piece.

clue.text: Duke's deputy found in strange locality

indicators.note: the answer is found lying within the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: The duke's deputy turns up in an odd place.
explanation.definitionFit: In Measure for Measure, Duke Vincentio leaves Angelo to rule Vienna in his absence.

clue.text: A tribe coming in after time to bring relief

indicators.note: one piece coming in to another enters its middle

parts.note: late means arriving after the expected time
Levi gave its name to one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: A tribe arrives, late, bringing aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after time' reads as a time phrase in the surface, but together it is a single synonym, for arriving overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain or distress is to ease or lessen it.

clue.text: River queen almost went up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run backwards
almost means the word stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A queen nearly climbed the river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims REGINA to REGIN; 'went up' turns it round to make NIGER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is West Africa's principal river, flowing through Mali and Nigeria.

clue.text: Being hanged after swallowing drug? That's very severe

indicators.note: one word taking another into its middle is said to be swallowing it

parts.note: a hanged body is left swinging from the rope
E is ecstasy, the party drug

explanation.surface: A grim scene: someone dosed with drugs and then executed, which is harsh indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is only a link word here; it does not order the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingeing cuts or penalties are punishingly harsh, a chiefly British adjective.

clue.text: Weapon sawn off by prisoner in camp

indicators.note: like a sawn-off shotgun, the word for the weapon loses its end

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a lag (old lag) is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A convict in a prison camp has a cut-down weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sawn off' trims the last letter from GUN, leaving GU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour camps, and the word now names any such camp.

clue.text: Hard way to become an astronomer

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an alley is a narrow way or passage

explanation.surface: Advice that the tough road leads to a career in stargazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Halley was the English scientist who predicted the return of the comet named after him.

clue.text: Traveller pins back ear to organ

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for ear in the opposite direction

parts.note: lug is informal British for an ear
the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A traveller listens hard, pinning back his ears to the sound of an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pins ... to' just joins the pieces: the backward LUG is pinned on to LIVER. The surface echoes 'pin back your ears', meaning listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemuel Gulliver is the much-travelled hero of Swift's satire Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Rebellion needs control: problem for propertied classes if it gets off the ground

definitions.text: problem for propertied classes if it gets off the ground

parts.note: a rising is an uprising or rebellion
to damp, as in damp down, is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A revolt must be suppressed before it gets going, or property owners suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'get off the ground' as both 'succeed' and literally climbing walls from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Moisture creeping up through a building's walls from the soil is a costly worry for householders.

clue.text: Man in charge of really fine mask

parts.note: super is an informal word for excellent or very fine
a visor is a face guard or mask, as on a helmet

explanation.surface: Praise for the boss's splendid mask.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor is the person who oversees workers, the one in charge of them.

clue.text: Having largest pot, I dipped into wine in case

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: a letter dipped into a word goes inside it

parts.note: lest means in case or for fear that

explanation.surface: A big-bellied drinker sticks his finger in his wine just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is a paunch, not a cooking pot or a jackpot; 'in case' is one synonym here, not an instruction to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly means stout, so the portliest person has the biggest belly; pot is slang for a paunch.

clue.text: Area shaded by tree is not dark

indicators.note: something in the shade of a tree sits beneath its covering, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a fir is a conifer

explanation.surface: A patch of ground under a tree's shade is still light.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair describes light hair or pale skin, the opposite of dark colouring.

clue.text: Ulster flag so described in the act

explanation.surface: A question about the flag of Northern Ireland and someone caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ulster banner bears a red hand, and to be caught with blood on one's hands means being caught committing a crime.

clue.text: Jargon is a lot of wind, in general

indicators.note: in places the word for winds inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
gales are strong winds

explanation.surface: Specialist talk is just hot air, generally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word. 'in general' looks like the phrase 'generally', but it means inside a general, LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers' language, dense with technical terms, is a classic example of impenetrable jargon.

clue.text: Fawn in European vineyard

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its classified wine

explanation.surface: A young deer wanders among the vines somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are pale greyish-yellow or beige shades, as of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Leader that's powerless, being bust from the navy

explanation.surface: A powerless leader is demoted out of the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal chief holds a title without real power, and a ship's prow traditionally carried a carved bust or figure.

clue.text: One stands for communist field-worker being a trimmer

explanation.surface: A communist farm labourer is tidy-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: On the hammer-and-sickle emblem the curved blade represents the peasantry, and it is also a tool for cutting grass or grain.

clue.text: Sinks, swallowing lieutenant in tidal area

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Sinks, swallowing lieutenant in tidal area (8)': LT inside a word for sinks would need SAINGS, which is no word; no source found giving the true clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sinks, swallowing lieutenant in tidal area

clue.text: Southern African is like that, however

parts.note: so means in that way, like that
tho, short for though, means however

explanation.surface: A remark that a southern African is just like that, though.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sotho are a Bantu people of Lesotho and South Africa.

clue.text: Principal river divides a harbour

indicators.note: a letter that splits a word in two sits inside it

parts.note: main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: The chief river runs through a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a purpose-built harbour for yachts and pleasure boats.

clue.text: Prophetic book's account shows patriarch

parts.note: Isa. is the abbreviation for the book of the prophet Isaiah
AC or a/c is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A biblical book's account presents one of the founding fathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham and father of Jacob, is one of the three biblical forefathers of Israel.

clue.text: Handwriting is used in newspaper

indicators.note: the word is put to use inside the newspaper's initials

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
taken as written

explanation.surface: Handwriting appears in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fist is old informal slang for a person's handwriting.

clue.text: Take wicket with spin, thus?

indicators.note: letters given spin are turned about into a new order

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket question: is this how a spin bowler takes a wicket?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to tweak the ball is to give it spin with the fingers, as a slow bowler does to take wickets; the whole clue is both recipe and description.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin bowler's twist of the fingers on the ball is a little turn, and that is how such a bowler hopes to dismiss a batsman.

clue.text: Amazingly, I balanced this on girl's head

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters end up in a surprising new arrangement

explanation.surface: A girl boasts of balancing something astonishing on her head.
explanation.definitionFit: This hair accessory is a flexible headband, named after the heroine in Tenniel's illustrations for Through the Looking-Glass.

clue.text: Challenged to get present

explanation.surface: Someone challenged to turn up in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Put on the spot means pressed for an immediate answer, and being on the spot also means being at the scene in person.

clue.text: The hero of the Spanish detectives?

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detective branch

explanation.surface: A question about which hero the Spanish police detectives worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodrigo Díaz, called El Cid, is the medieval Castilian warrior celebrated as Spain's national champion.
